sentence: POST /api/waterings with litres set to boolean true is accepted with 201 and stored as 1.0 litres.
evidence: Signed in as the demo user via POST /api/auth/login, then sent POST /api/waterings {"bed_id":1,"litres":true}. The API returned 201 with {"id":3,"bed_id":1,"bed_name":"North bed","watered_on":"2026-11-12",...,"litres":1.0}, and GET /api/waterings then listed that row as a stored 1.0 L watering. With litres:false the same request got 422 (greater_than 0), which shows the boolean is being turned into a number rather than rejected as the wrong type. Cause: WateringIn.litres is declared as `float | None` in Pydantic lax mode (backend/schemas.py:131) with no strict typing, so true is coerced to 1.0. A boolean is not a valid amount in litres, so the API should reject it with 422; instead it stores made-up data. The UI form does not send booleans, so only direct API clients can trigger this.
